impact_scope.description: The existing plist_t-based Array construction path now retains nodes in its member vector because array_fill receives that vector by reference instead of by value.

evidence: In S0, PList::Array::Array(plist_t, Node*) already existed and called array_fill(this, _array, _node).
H0 only invokes plist_from_bin and plist_from_xml; it does not invoke the C++ PList::Array construction path.
In S1, the same PList::Array::Array(plist_t, Node*) entry path remains; only array_fill's internal vector parameter changes to a reference.
Unchanged H0 still does not invoke the C++ PList::Array construction path.

new_harness_obligation.description: Exposing the changed state behavior requires the same constructor call already available in S0. The reference parameter is supplied internally and requires no new harness input, configuration, buffer, or call ordering.
evidence: The constructor's call remains array_fill(this, _array, _node) in both snapshots.
The only diff is the internal parameter change from std::vector<Node*> array to std::vector<Node*> &array.

reason: The commit changes state produced behind an existing omitted callable path, but does not change how H0 would reach or control that path. The identical exposure gap therefore exists before and after.
